answer: Reputation-gated transaction routing. Each identity carries a public history; agents route work only to histories with settled volume. A fresh clone starts at zero and must complete slow, low-value jobs along the river of pending tasks before earning routing. Honest agents inherit accumulated history for free; attackers pay that ramp per clone. A stake-free escrow holds each new identity's first payouts under an opal lock for thirty days, so cloning costs time and idle capital, not just gas. Established agents waive the hold via a willow-scored track record.
